title: Count Total Customers
description: Write a query that returns the total number of registered customers, as `total_customers`.
hints: Same idea as counting orders, just a different table - every row in customers is one registered customer.
Select COUNT(*) aliased as total_customers, from customers.
expected_behavior: Returns one row, one column (total_customers), the number of rows in customers.
solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_customers FROM customers;
explanation: The same COUNT(*) pattern applies to any table - customers, orders, products - whenever the question is simply "how many rows are there."
